analysis.overview: BIOC3111 provides a comprehensive introduction to modern protein science, building on BIOC2101 and BIOC2201. Lectures cover protein structure and function, analytical tools, protein-protein interactions, folding, engineering, and proteomics. A 10-week practical project develops experimental design, purification and characterisation skills with embedded scientific communication training. Core to the Molecular and Cell Biology Major; 6 UOC, Term 2, multimodal delivery at Kensington.

topics.title: Protein Sequences, Evolution and Bioinformatics
learning_outcomes: Explain protein sequence, evolution and post-translational modification concepts
Explain bioinformatics approaches used in protein analysis
topics.source_evidence: Weeks 1-2 lectures: Protein Evolution, Bioinformatics, Post Translational Modifications

topics.title: Protein Folding, Stability and Chaperones
learning_outcomes: Explain principles of protein folding and stability
Relate misfolding to amyloid diseases and chaperone function
topics.source_evidence: Week 3 lectures: Folding and Stability, Amyloid Diseases, Molecular Chaperones

topics.title: Protein Interactions, Motors and Assemblies
learning_outcomes: Explain protein-protein interactions and molecular motor mechanisms
Describe protein assemblies in infection and therapeutic design
topics.source_evidence: Weeks 4 and 9 lectures: Molecular Motors, Protein-Protein Interactions, Protein Assemblies

topics.title: Proteomics and the Human Proteome
learning_outcomes: Explain proteomics as large-scale study of cellular proteins
Describe the Human Proteome Project and clinical proteomics applications
topics.source_evidence: Week 5 lectures: Proteomics I-II, Human Proteome Project, Clinical Proteomics

topics.title: Mass Spectrometry and Biophysics
learning_outcomes: Explain mass spectrometry methods for protein characterisation
Explain biophysical techniques in protein analysis
topics.source_evidence: Week 7 lectures: Mass Spectrometry I-II, Biophysics

topics.title: Structural Biology and Structure Prediction
learning_outcomes: Explain structural biology methods including cryo-EM
Describe machine learning approaches to structure prediction
topics.source_evidence: Week 8 lectures: Structural Biology Methods, Cryo-EM, Machine Learning Prediction

topics.title: Protein Function and Engineering
subtopics: Protein function as a physical process
learning_outcomes: Link protein structure to function as a physical process
topics.source_evidence: Weeks 9-10 lectures: Structure to Function, Protein Function, Protein Engineering

study_notes: Students must attempt all assessment tasks to pass; practical attendance is compulsory and missing more than one class may result in an Unsatisfactory Fail.
Complete the BABS Health & Safety Quiz (100%) before the first practical class on Tuesday 2 June 2026 and bring a screenshot to show your demonstrator.
Bring your own PPE (lab coat, safety glasses, enclosed shoes) and a laptop with Safe Exam Browser installed for Inspera assessments.
The Early Bird Test covers Weeks 1-3 lecture material; practice questions and model responses are provided on Moodle.
A supplementary Final Exam, if special consideration is approved, runs 7-11 September 2026 with no alternative dates.
